svg.title: A $60,000 Asset-Light Startup Allocation
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-startup-capital-allocation; chart type: stacked_comparison; title: A $60,000 Asset-Light Startup Allocation; subtitle: Four cash buckets fit inside the canonical $10,000–$75,000 startup range.; chapter number: 4; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Numeric values are USD allocations totaling $60,000. This is one illustrative capitalization plan, not a prescribed minimum. Cash reserves are not immediate expenses; spending enters the appropriate operating category when incurred. Do not add these allocations again to the annual expense waterfall.; caption: $36,000 + $8,000 + $10,000 + $6,000 = $60,000. The $36,000 recurring-overhead reserve covers nine months at $4,000 monthly before revenue, matching the upper end of the canonical two-to-nine-month first-deal window. Other spending uses the remaining buckets and must be paced separately.; stages: label: Recurring-overhead reserve; value: $36,000 reserved for nine months of recurring operations; numeric value: 36000.0; detail: Hold this cash against the Base overhead assumption of $4,000 monthly. It excludes owner household spending and variable closing costs. Track actual runway weekly because late commissions can arrive after bills fall due.; label: Field verification capacity; value: $8,000 allocated to early inspections and ownership evidence; numeric value: 8000.0; detail: Fund initial specialist inspections, title and filing searches, equipment photography, and necessary site visits. Require asset-specific scopes and stop spending when a seller cannot establish authority or access.; label: Seller and buyer acquisition; value: $10,000 allocated to targeted sourcing and qualified outreach; numeric value: 10000.0; detail: Support focused trade-directory research, targeted seller outreach, buyer qualification, and selected industry visits. Release spending in small batches against mandate and buyer-match evidence rather than committing the full budget to broad advertising.; label: Systems and transaction setup; value: $6,000 allocated to equipment records and settlement readiness; numeric value: 6000.0; detail: Configure Airtable asset records, HubSpot workflows, document templates, e-signature, and secure file access. Establish escrow-provider verification and bookkeeping categories. Purchase no equipment inventory and advance no buyer purchase principal from this allocation.

rect.title: label: Recurring-overhead reserve; numeric value: 36000.0; value: $36,000 reserved for nine months of recurring operations; detail: Hold this cash against the Base overhead assumption of $4,000 monthly. It excludes owner household spending and variable closing costs. Track actual runway weekly because late commissions can arrive after bills fall due.

rect.title: label: Field verification capacity; numeric value: 8000.0; value: $8,000 allocated to early inspections and ownership evidence; detail: Fund initial specialist inspections, title and filing searches, equipment photography, and necessary site visits. Require asset-specific scopes and stop spending when a seller cannot establish authority or access.

Release spending in small batches against mandate and buyer-match evidence rather than committing the full budget to broad advertising.

Establish escrow-provider verification and bookkeeping categories. Purchase no equipment inventory and advance no buyer purchase principal from this allocation.
